research:
Web finds:
I found 8 leads, but only 3 are clearly inside the 7-day window, and none comes with a verified view count from this week. The searches mostly returned undated tag pages and trend blogs. Each entry says how sure the date and numbers are.

- **Scam calls answered on Mum's landline, in a posh 1920s voice.** Inside the window: no, 14 days old.
  - **Where:** Instagram and TikTok. The Know Your Meme write-up is dated Nov 5.
  - **Creator:** JJ Kirwan, an Irish comedian.
  - **Numbers:** a search summary of the Yahoo/Know Your Meme piece said about 10.2M views on Instagram and 4.9M on TikTok in 6 days. The Know Your Meme page itself shows no count, so this is unconfirmed.
  - **What happens:** the caption is "POV: your mother still has a landline, so this is how you answer scam calls." He answers on a gold, old-style receiver in an exaggerated old-fashioned British accent, then hangs up with an old-timey sound effect. The punchline is him telling his mum in his normal voice that he hung up because she kept talking.
  - **Why it spread:** everyone gets scam calls and everyone has a parent with a landline. You get to beat the scammer without any risk.
  - **Fit:** strong for MUM VS AI. It could also be a REAL FIX with a "hang up and call back on the number you already have" rule.

- **Toddler and his pet goat watching videos on a phone together.** Inside the window: yes.
  - **Where:** Instagram, account rozkascen, Nov 13.
  - **Numbers:** 371.4K likes in 22 hours, per MENAFN.
  - **What happens:** a mum shares her toddler's screen-time struggle. He pulls the goat in, and the two sit side by side staring at reels.
  - **Why it spread:** it's a cute screen-time confession every parent recognises.
  - **Fit:** loose. A possible "the committee is binge-watching on Meera's phone" or screen-time angle.

- **An AI maintenance chatbot tells a tenant their apartment doesn't exist.** Inside the window: yes, as a screenshot.
  - **Where:** Yahoo's "27 hilarious fails from last week" roundup, about 2 days old. It's a screenshot, not a video.
  - **Numbers:** none given. I couldn't confirm the incident anywhere else.
  - **What happens:** the tenant reports no heat, and the bot confidently says the apartment isn't real.
  - **Why it spread:** it's the confident wrong answer, at the worst moment.
  - **Fit:** our "confident, made-up answers" truth rule, in a landlord or bills story. It's thin as a source, so use only the shape, not the specifics.

- **Viewer stories of things caught on camera during work calls.** Inside the window: unclear, probably no.
  - **Where:** TikTok, from a Yahoo article dated Nov 18. The creator's handle isn't in the snippet. The article mentions @taylormakesvideos reacting on Nov 6 to comments on a @flippinpallets video, so that clip is 13 days old.
  - **Numbers:** none given.
  - **What happens:** a creator reads out viewers' stories. One is about a dad on a Teams call whose kid interrupts, and the boss replies with a dry one-liner.
  - **Why it spread:** people share their own "this happened on my call" stories.
  - **Fit:** OFFICE WITH AI, for example Gemini quietly unmuting or sharing the wrong screen.

- **"Scarf Man" at Seoul's Namdaemun market tells customers not to buy.** Inside the window: borderline.
  - **Where:** short videos, from a CNN report on Nov 14/15.
  - **Numbers:** hundreds of people queue at his shop. The first batch in his new online store sold out within 24 hours. There's no view count.
  - **What happens:** the more he talks people out of buying, the more they buy.
  - **Why it spread:** reverse psychology is funny, and honesty is a twist people don't expect.
  - **Fit:** a Mitti shop episode where Claude politely talks every customer out of buying, and the orders go up.

- **"Add to Cart" format.** Inside the window: November roundup, no exact date.
  - **Where:** Instagram, from the NewEngen weekly trends page.
  - **Numbers:** none.
  - **What happens:** hands keep pushing products into the frame, each gets an "add to cart" moment, and it ends on the full pile or the checkout screen. The roundup suggests 8 to 15 seconds.
  - **Why it spread:** holiday sales and gift guides.
  - **Fit:** Gemini "helpfully" adding things to Meera's cart one after another, with the twin adding the total.

- **"Lately on my SD card" format.** Inside the window: from a roundup about 5 days old.
  - **Where:** Instagram, from the NapoleonCat and Lightreel November reports.
  - **Numbers:** none.
  - **What happens:** an SD card graphic with the title text, then a quick flick through recent clips and photos.
  - **Fit:** a remake as "lately in my chat history", a quick run of the absurd things Meera asked the AIs this week.

- **Indian dad thinks the "Korean heart" finger gesture means money and gives his daughter Rs 500.** Inside the window: no, the clip is undated, probably old.
  - **Where:** Instagram, from Tribune India.
  - **Numbers:** over 70.4M views.
  - **What happens:** the daughter makes the trendy heart gesture, the dad reads it as "give me cash" and hands her Rs 500.
  - **Why it spread:** parents misreading internet culture.
  - **Fit:** MUM VS AI, with Mum misreading what a chatbot or AI word means. Only use it if you're fine with an evergreen pick.

**What I skipped:**
- Political, or mocking a real person: Andy Burnham's ChatGPT joke at PMQs (Nov 18) and the AI memes about Jensen Huang's scandal (Nov 14).
- Not comedy: the Indian parents' first-flight video and a daughter's Diwali surprise.
- Undated or older: the ChatGPT roast-my-profile challenge, "you're absolutely right" skits, and the ChatGPT graduation clips.

**Gap:** I couldn't find a dated viral AI-assistant skit from this week with numbers. Before picking, check YouTube Shorts and TikTok search sorted by "this week" in the app.

remakes.creator: JJ Kirwan (internal only, never named in the episode or caption)
remakes.numbers: About 10.2M views on Instagram and 4.9M on TikTok in 6 days, from a search summary of the Yahoo and Know Your Meme piece. This is unconfirmed: the KYM page shows no count. It was posted around 5 Nov, so it is 14 days old and outside the 7-day window. There is no channel median, so no outlier multiple can be computed. I still chose it because it is by far the biggest reported signal and the most natural fit for the committee. The only in-window find with verified velocity, the toddler and goat clip (371K likes in 22 h), fits the committee only loosely. The 'apartment doesn't exist' chatbot item has no numbers and is a screenshot, not a video.
remakes.what_happens: A man answers scam calls on his mum's landline in an absurd, exaggerated old-fashioned character, ruins the scammer's script and hangs up. The final beat flips back to his mum in his normal voice.
remakes.why_it_worked: Everyone gets scam calls and everyone has a parent who answers them. Viewers enjoy seeing the scammer beaten with zero risk, and the family twist at the end makes it shareable ('send this to Mum').
remakes.our_twist:
Instead of one comic character, we have three real AI personalities picking up. Codex is literal, Claude is too kind and gives therapy plus a five-page career plan, and Gemini adds an unrequested podcast and sends it on. The scammer gets out-talked, not out-smarted, and the punchline is Mum's Hinglish text saying he only wants to talk to 'the orange one'.

It is pure comedy like the original, so it has no keyword and no fix. Scam topics have aired often lately, so this one takes a comedy angle and gives no fix or advice. It is affectionate to Claude fans, and the joke lands on AI behaviour, not on Mum or any group.
